docs.title: Hyperbolix
docs.text:
Hyperbolic Deep Learning in JAX

Hyperbolix is a pure JAX implementation of hyperbolic deep learning, providing manifold operations, neural network layers, and Riemannian optimizers for hyperbolic geometry. Built with Flax NNX and Optax for modern JAX workflows.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 6 Manifolds: Euclidean, Poincaré Ball, Hyperboloid, Proper Velocity, κ-Stereographic (signed curvature — hyperbolic, flat, and spherical in one manifold), and Product Manifold (mixed-curvature composition) — all with complete geometric operations
  • Learnable Curvature: LearnableCurvature module bundles parameter + reparameterization (softplus, log/exp, or signed identity) + optional clamp; works with any nnx.Optimizer
  • Neural Network Layers: 40+ hyperbolic layers including linear, convolutional, regression, attention, normalization, and PV layers
  • Activation Functions: 5 hyperbolic activations (ReLU, Leaky ReLU, Tanh, Swish, GELU)
  • Riemannian Optimizers: RAdam and RSGD with automatic manifold parameter detection
  • Wrapped Normal Distributions: For probabilistic modeling on hyperbolic manifolds
  • Dimensionality Reduction: HoroPCA (Chami et al. 2021), CO-SNE (Guo et al. 2022, hyperbolic t-SNE), and the Fréchet-mean centering primitive — hyperbolic analogues of PCA and t-SNE
  • Pure JAX/Flax NNX: No PyTorch dependency, fully compatible with JAX ecosystem
  • vmap-native API: Efficient batching through JAX's functional paradigm
  • JIT-compatible: All operations support JIT compilation for performance
  • Comprehensive Test Suite: 4,000+ tests (parametrized across dtypes, dimensions, manifolds) checked against independently transcribed NumPy/SciPy oracles

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from hyperbolix.manifolds import Poincare

# Create manifold (float32 by default, float64 for higher precision)
poincare = Poincare()

# Create points on the Poincaré ball
x = jnp.array([0.1, 0.2])
y = jnp.array([0.3, -0.1])
c = 1.0  # Curvature parameter

# Compute distance (single point operation)
distance = poincare.dist(x, y, c)
print(f"Distance: {distance}")

# Batch operations with vmap
x_batch = jax.random.normal(jax.random.PRNGKey(0), (100, 2)) * 0.3
y_batch = jax.random.normal(jax.random.PRNGKey(1), (100, 2)) * 0.3

# Project to manifold and compute pairwise distances
x_proj = jax.vmap(poincare.proj, in_axes=(0, None))(x_batch, c)
y_proj = jax.vmap(poincare.proj, in_axes=(0, None))(y_batch, c)
distances = jax.vmap(poincare.dist, in_axes=(0, 0, None))(x_proj, y_proj, c)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install from source:

git clone https://github.com/timoklein/hyperbolix.git
cd hyperbolix
uv sync  # or pip install -e .

Requirements: Python 3.12+, JAX, Flax NNX, Optax

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Hyperbolix follows a class-based manifold design with functional transformations:

# Manifold classes with automatic dtype casting
from hyperbolix.manifolds import Poincare
import jax.numpy as jnp

poincare = Poincare(dtype=jnp.float64)  # Optional float64 precision
distance = poincare.dist(x, y, c=1.0)

# Neural network layers as Flax NNX modules
from flax import nnx
from hyperbolix.nn_layers import HypLinearPoincare

model = HypLinearPoincare(
    manifold_module=poincare,
    in_dim=32,
    out_dim=16,
    rngs=nnx.Rngs(0)
)
output = model(input_data, c=1.0)

docs.title: vmap-native API
docs.text:
Methods operate on single points by design. Use jax.vmap for batching:

poincare = Poincare()

# Single point operation
result = poincare.expmap(x, v, c)

# Batched operation
batch_result = jax.vmap(poincare.expmap, in_axes=(0, 0, None))(x_batch, v_batch, c)

This design enables efficient JIT compilation and clear semantics.

docs.title: Curvature Parameter
docs.text:
The curvature c is passed at call time, not stored in the manifold:

poincare = Poincare()

# Different curvatures for different calls
dist_c1 = poincare.dist(x, y, c=1.0)
dist_c2 = poincare.dist(x, y, c=2.0)

docs.title: Learnable Curvature
docs.text:
Curvature can be made trainable via the LearnableCurvature module. Instantiate one per distinct curvature in your model and call it at runtime:

from hyperbolix import LearnableCurvature
from hyperbolix.manifolds import Hyperboloid

class Model(nnx.Module):
    def __init__(self, rngs):
        self.manifold = Hyperboloid(c=1.0)
        self.curvature = LearnableCurvature(init_c=1.0)  # nnx.Module on the model
        self.fc = FGGLinear(33, 65, rngs=rngs)

    def __call__(self, x):
        c = self.curvature()                             # positive, clamped to [0.1, 10.0]
        return self.fc(x, c=c)

Pick parameterization="log" for compiled RL loops or when c spans orders of magnitude; the default "softplus" is best for supervised training, and "identity" gives a signed curvature for the Stereographic manifold. See the Manifolds guide for details.

docs.title: Mixed-Curvature Product Spaces
docs.text:
Compose heterogeneous factors (each with its own curvature) into a single product manifold (Gu et al. 2019). Curvature is supplied at call time as a per-factor sequence — pass product.curvatures for static factors, or build the sequence from LearnableCurvature calls for trainable factors:

from hyperbolix.manifolds import ProductManifold, Hyperboloid, Poincare, Euclidean

product = ProductManifold(
    (Hyperboloid(c=1.0), 5),   # hyperbolic factor
    (Poincare(c=0.1), 3),      # Poincaré factor
    (Euclidean(), 4),          # flat factor
)
c = product.curvatures               # (1.0, 0.1, 0.0)
d = product.dist(x, y, c)            # sqrt(sum d_i^2) over factors

docs.title: Manifold Operations
docs.text:
Each manifold provides:

  • proj: Project points onto the manifold
  • dist: Compute distances (multiple versions for numerical stability)
  • expmap/logmap: Exponential and logarithmic maps
  • ptransp: Parallel transport
  • egrad2rgrad: Convert Euclidean to Riemannian gradients

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to Hyperbolix will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Every zero-initialised hyperboloid gyro-bias was frozen at its init value: ∂(x ⊕ b)/∂b at b = origin was exactly the zero matrix, in both dtypes. dist_0 short-circuited on a bitwise at_origin guard (jnp.where(at_origin, 0.0, res)); logmap_0 scales the spatial part by dist_0(y)/‖y_s‖ and inherited it; Lorentz gyro addition x ⊕ y = Exp_x(PT_{0→x}(Log_0(y))) inherited it in turn. A bias parameter that starts at the origin, which is what use_gyro_bias=True does, therefore received an exactly-zero gradient at step 0 and never left. Affected layers: HypLinearHyperboloidPLFC, HypConv2DHyperboloidILNN, HypLinearHyperboloidBusemann. Measured gyro-bias gradient L2 at init (c = 1, dim 8, batch 4, dist_0 loss, before → after): float32 0.0 → 1.37 (PLFC), 0.0 → 4.24 (ILNN conv), 0.0 → 3.07 (Busemann FC); float64 0.0 → 1.48, 0.0 → 5.37, 0.0 → 1.83. In float32 the gradient was additionally ~1400x over-scaled the moment the bias left the origin, because the acosh floor below was divided by the true radius: the PLFC gradient at bias radius 1e-6 was 1535x its value at 1e-2, a ratio that is now 1.06x. The Poincaré HypLinearPoincareBusemann gyro-bias goes through Möbius addition and was never affected (7.64 before and after). A model trained with a gyro-bias on any of the three hyperboloid layers was trained with that bias pinned to the origin; retraining under this fix changes results.

  • Hyperboloid dist_0/logmap_0 recovered the geodesic radius from the time coordinate x₀, which cannot resolve a small radius; they now read it off the spatial part. dist_0 was acosh(clip(√c·x₀, 1))/√c. On the sheet x₀ = cosh(√c·d)/√c ≈ (1 + c·d²/2)/√c, so d survives only to sqrt(eps) resolution (relative error eps/(2·c·d²)), and acosh's 1 + 10·eps domain clamp flattened every float32 radius below sqrt(20·eps)/√c = 1.5441e-3 onto that floor value (1.5441e-3 was returned for every such point, 1500x too large at radius 1e-6; only the bitwise origin returned 0). The smoothened arm was worse: smooth_clamp_min (β = 50) adds ln2/50 to the acosh argument, i.e. a floor of acosh(1 + ln2/50)/√c = 0.16632/√c under every point that is not bitwise the origin, in both dtypes (measured: it returned 0.16632 at every radius ≤ 1e-2 and 0.1815 at radius 0.1, agreeing with the true value only from radius ≈ 1). Slot 0 is now the exact on-sheet identity arcsinh(√c·‖x_s‖)/√c, with no domain clamp and a derivative bounded by 1; slot 1 is the same with the spatial radius floored in quadrature at 20·eps, a floor of arcsinh(20·eps)/√c (2.4e-6/√c float32, 4.4e-15/√c float64) that equals the pairwise smoothened floor 2·arcsinh(10·eps)/√c from 1.1.2 to first order. logmap_0 is now [0, arcsinh(u)/u · y_s] with u = √c‖y_s‖: it no longer routes through dist_0's version switch, ‖log_0(y)‖ = dist_0(y) holds by construction instead of by cancelling a floored numerator against an unfloored denominator, and the trailing tangent_proj is dropped (it is the identity at the origin, but it routes through the Minkowski inner product, which turns one inf spatial coordinate into an all-NaN vector). scalar_mul is now literally exp_0(r · log_0(x)); its old normalize-then-rescale detour carried a sqrt(max(‖v‖², MIN_NORM)) floor, an effective 3.16e-8 floor on ‖log_0 x‖ that was invisible only while the larger acosh floor sat in front of it. Median relative error at c = 1, dim 8 (A100, jax 0.9.1; the CPU backend and jax 0.11.0 agree in every floored cell):

    radius float32 dist_0 float32 log_0(exp_0(v)) float64 dist_0 float64 round trip 1e-6 1.5e3 → 2.5e-9 1.5e3 → 0 4.4e-5 → 0 4.4e-5 → 1.3e-16 1e-3 5.4e-1 → 9.8e-8 5.4e-1 → 0 5.9e-11 → 0 1.5e-10 → 1.2e-16 1e-2 5.0e-4 → 2.7e-8 5.2e-4 → 0 1.0e-12 → 1.7e-16 8.3e-13 → 1.2e-16 0.1 3.5e-6 → 1.8e-8 1.4e-7 → 3.9e-8 7.6e-15 → 1.4e-16 9.5e-15 → 1.1e-16 1 to 40 ≤7.1e-8 → ≤5.2e-8 ≤1.0e-7 → ≤8.8e-8 ≤1.3e-16 → ≤1.9e-16 ≤1.4e-16 → ≤1.4e-16

    Consumers that inherit the fix with no change of their own: gyro addition, scalar_mul, logmap's origin fallback, HyperboloidGyroRMSNorm (it divides by dist_0, so in float32 every sample inside radius 1.5e-3 was mis-normalised), and the three gyro-bias layers above. Pairwise dist(origin, x) is a separate code path and still carries an O(eps/r) relative error from the _polar_frame gap term near the origin (float32: 4.6e-2 at radius 1e-6, ~1e-3 at 1e-4); closing that is a planned separate change, so prefer dist_0 for distances to the origin. Supersedes the claim in the 1.1.2 entry below that origin-chart operations "read the radius straight off the ambient time coordinate and were never affected": reading it off the time coordinate is precisely the defect fixed here. That entry's two-point cancellation claims, and expmap_0, are unchanged

  • On an Ampere or Hopper GPU, lorentz_midpoint and the three hyperbolic attention layers silently ran their matmuls in TF32, costing ~2000x accuracy in the one place the library cannot afford it. XLA:GPU defaults float32 matmuls to TF32, whose 10-bit mantissa carries ~1e-3 relative error against float32's ~1e-7. lorentz_midpoint's whole design is a cancellation-free identity in which every rounded term is O(‖delta‖²), so that the normalizer stays accurate at any radius — TF32 is far coarser than the effect that identity exists to remove. Measured float32-vs-float64 relative error of lorentz_midpoint (A100, jax 0.9.1, c ∈ {0.1, 1.0} × ‖s‖ ∈ {0.5, 5, 20}): GPU default 4.6e-5 … 2.6e-4, GPU with the fix 2.6e-8 … 1.6e-7, CPU 2.6e-8 … 1.2e-7 — i.e. three of the seven significant digits were gone, with no warning, in every hyperbolic attention or Fréchet-mean computation on such a card. The worst site is HyperbolicFullAttention's Lorentzian similarity, which evaluates ⟨Q,K⟩_L = -Q₀K₀ + ⟨Q_s,K_s⟩ as the difference of two matmuls — the exact cancellation _polar_frame was written to avoid, with both halves produced by TF32 GEMMs, so the subtraction amplifies a ~1e-3 input error rather than a ~1e-7 one. Fixed by annotating the cancellation-sensitive dots with precision=jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST through one documented constant, hyperbolix.nn_layers.hyperboloid_core.MATMUL_PRECISION: the three jnp.einsums in lorentz_midpoint, the ten score / Lorentz-inner-product / aggregate einsums in hyperboloid_attention.py, the spatial residual projection the linear and softmax variants add to that aggregate, and HTCLinear's matmul — the last because it produces the Q/K/V the Lorentz inner product then cancels, and a TF32 input makes an accurate cancellation pointless (annotating only the attention einsums left 6 of the 7 attention tests red; adding HTCLinear left 2; adding the residual projection cleared them). This turned 14 of the 21 GPU-only test failures green (all 7 attention, all 7 lorentz_midpoint). HIGHEST is a no-op on CPU (no TF32 path) and for float64 anywhere; the CPU outputs of lorentz_midpoint and of a HyperbolicFullAttention forward are bit-identical before and after, eager and jitted, in both dtypes. On a tensor-core GPU it does trade GEMM throughput for accuracy, since HIGHEST replaces one TF32 pass with a three-pass float32 emulation: a jitted HyperbolicFullAttention forward at B = 8, N = 256, 4 heads, head dim 64, float32 measured a median 1.84 ms with the fix vs 1.74 ms at the TF32 default, +5.5 % (A100-PCIE-40GB, 5 warmup + 20 timed calls; the card was idle but shared, so treat the ratio as indicative)

  • The hyperboloid MLR forward dot ran in TF32 on the same cards, for the same reason: _compute_mlr forms alpha = -x₀·sinh(√c·r)·‖z‖ + cosh(√c·r)·⟨x_s, z⟩, a difference whose second term is a matmul. The einsum now carries precision=HIGHEST (spelled out locally — manifolds/ must not import from nn_layers/). Measured on an A100 against a float64 reference at identical inputs: the eager float32 gradient of _compute_mlr improves from 1.5e-4 to 2.7e-7 relative; the forward was already accurate (1.1e-7) on both settings. This does not fix the separate, intermittent 1 % error in the jitted float32 gradient of the same function, which survives every precision setting; that one is the jnp.maximum tie-break in the next entry
  • The remaining float32 dots on manifold data still ran in TF32 on Ampere/Hopper — the x @ V matmuls where the Minkowski metric is absorbed into the weight matrix, and the HoroPCA and Poincaré-MLR contractions. PR #70 closed the Lorentz cancellations that are written as an explicit difference of two dots (lorentz_midpoint, the attention scores, the hyperboloid MLR); this closes the rest. FGGLinear, FGGLorentzMLR and HypRegressionHyperboloid evaluate ⟨x, V⟩_L as one x @ V with the metric folded into V, so the -x₀V₀ + ⟨x_s, V_s⟩ cancellation happens inside a single TF32 accumulation and the ~1e-3 input rounding lands directly on the cancelled result. Measured float32-vs-float64 relative error on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, ambient dim 33, batch 64, c ∈ {0.1, 1.0} × spatial radius ∈ {0.5, 5, 20}; median over the batch, before → after): FGGLinear 2.6e-4 → 6.8e-8 (a 3700-3900x improvement at every cell), FGGLorentzMLR 1.3e-4 … 3.6e-4 → 3.6e-8 … 9.6e-8 (2200-3800x), horo_projection 4.0e-4 … 4.9e-3 → 2.8e-7 … 2.4e-6 (1400-2600x, the ideal-span Minkowski projections), HoroPCA.transform 1.9e-4 … 2.3e-3 → 3.4e-7 … 4.3e-6 (520-1560x, the Fréchet-mean Lorentz boost x @ Bᵀ plus the component-frame read-off), and the Poincaré HNN++ MLR compute_mlr_pp 3.8e-5 … 1.4e-4 → 6.0e-8 … 2.2e-7 (440-1740x). The fix is one library-wide setting rather than a per-call keyword: MATMUL_PRECISION = jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST now lives in hyperbolix.utils.precision — a neutral home both manifolds/ and nn_layers/ can import from, so manifolds/hyperboloid.py::_compute_mlr imports it instead of spelling lax.Precision.HIGHEST locally — and is attached to all 87 float32 dot products in the package that touch points, tangent vectors or hyperplane normals (70 of them newly). hyperbolix.nn_layers.hyperboloid_core.MATMUL_PRECISION re-exports it, so existing imports keep working unchanged. Covered: the Poincaré/κ-stereographic/proper-velocity/gyrovector-core jnp.dot reductions behind dist, addition, gyration, expmap, logmap, ptransp, tangent_inner, egrad2rgrad and the boundary factors 1 - c‖x‖²; the hyperboloid _minkowski_inner, _proj time reconstruction, polar-frame Gram-Schmidt, tangent_norm radial split and Busemann coordinate; the isometry maps between the three models; HypLinearHyperboloidFHCNN/FHNN and HypLinearPoincare's tangent-space matmuls; the Poincaré batch-norm weighted gyromidpoint; HypVQMLRPoincare's implicit-codebook matmul; and the hyperboloid/Poincaré/PV conv patch extraction (conv_general_dilated_patches carries ambient channels, time slot included). HIGHEST is a no-op on CPU and for float64 anywhere, and the change is verified bit-identical: 280 CPU arrays covering every touched public entry point, forward and jax.grad, eager and jitted, in both dtypes, match the base commit exactly. The single-vector jnp.dot sites measured no GPU change either way (XLA lowers a vector-vector dot to a reduction rather than a tensor-core GEMM), so those annotations are insurance against a future lowering or a batched rewrite rather than a behaviour change today
  • The ‖z‖ floor in the hyperboloid MLR silently zeroed the entire ∂‖z‖ branch of its gradient on GPU, for one output channel at a time, in roughly two of every three process launches. _compute_mlr floored the hyperplane-normal norm with jnp.linalg.norm(z, ...).clip(min=min_enorm), i.e. jnp.maximum(n, eps). That op's JVP is jax's tie-breaking _balanced_eq, g · [n == ans] / (1 + [eps == ans]) — it tests the operand n for bit equality with the result ans, which is sound only while the two are literally the same value in the compiled graph. XLA:GPU emits n = sqrt(sum(z*z)) twice in the compiled backward — once as its own small fusion, once recomputed inside the fusion that evaluates the ∂‖z‖ branch — and its per-process fusion autotuner picks the emitter for the first one by measured runtime, NATIVE_EMITTER or BLOCK_LEVEL_EMITTER (Triton). The two emitters disagree in the last bit of n for some rows; when they do, [n == ans] is false for that row, the derivative factor becomes 0, and the gradient returned for that output channel is exactly the one you would get by treating ‖z‖ as a constant. Measured on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, linear_plfc layer-contract inputs, float32 vs a float64 reference): jitted gradient relative error 1.0e-2 → 1.5e-7, and in a failing launch the affected row matched the ‖z‖-frozen gradient to 2.5e-8 while every other row was correct to 1.5e-7 — the branch was dropped, not perturbed. The reduced repro failed in 5 of 8 launches before and passed 7 of 7 after; test_gradient_contract[linear_plfc-f32] failed in 3 of 4 pytest launches before and passed 3 of 3 after. This was not conditioning: perturbing ‖z‖ by one float32 ulp in float64 — coherently, or independently at each of its three occurrences in the formula — moves the true gradient by at most 2.4e-7, five orders of magnitude short of the observed error. The floor is now jnp.where(n > min_enorm, n, min_enorm), which compares n against the constant (0.027 vs 1e-15 at these inputs) instead of against a differently-rounded copy of itself, so no 1-ulp disagreement can flip it. Forward values and the CPU gradient are bit-identical before and after in both dtypes, eager and jitted; only a NaN z behaves differently (maximum propagates the NaN, where floors it), which is already outside the function's contract. Flooring the squared sum instead (sqrt(maximum(Σz², eps²))) does not help — it keeps the same maximum tie-break and still failed 4 of 6 launches. The three XLA flags that hid the symptom (--xla_gpu_enable_cublaslt=false, --xla_gpu_autotune_level=0, --xla_gpu_enable_triton_gemm=false) each did so only by removing the emitter choice, not by fixing anything. The same hazard applies to every jnp.maximum(f(x), floor) on a differentiated path — the library has ~30 such MIN_NORM floors — but only this one has been observed to fire; a pure-JAX repro and a draft upstream report are in logs/2026-09-03_plfc_jit_grad/upstream/
  • The same GPU gradient-zeroing hazard is now closed at every other constant floor and clamp in the library — 76 sites. The mechanism is the one in the entry above: jnp.maximum(f(x), CONST)'s JVP is jax's _balanced_eq, which tests the operand for bit equality with the result, and XLA:GPU may compute the operand twice with emitters chosen per process by its fusion autotuner. When the two copies disagree by 1 ulp the whole gradient branch through the operand is silently zeroed. Only the MLR site had been observed to fire, but every constant floor on a differentiated path is exposed, so all of them are rewritten as a comparison against the constant, through three new one-line helpers in hyperbolix.utils.math_utils: floor_at(x, lo) = where(x < lo, lo, x), cap_at(x, hi) = where(x > hi, hi, x), and clamp_to(x, lo, hi) = cap_at(floor_at(x, lo), hi). The comparison direction is chosen so a NaN operand still propagates exactly as maximum/minimum/clip propagated it (NaN < lo is false, so the NaN is selected), which makes the forward value identical for every input — finite, NaN, and ±inf — at all 76 sites, in both dtypes, eager and jitted. Converted: the whole of manifolds/ (hyperboloid 23, poincaré 6, gyrovector core 8, stereographic 4, proper velocity 2, product 1, isometry mappings 3), distributions/ (2), decomposition/ (9), utils/ (8), and nn_layers/ (10). Deliberately not converted (9 sites): the smooth_clamp family, where the 0.5/0.5 tie split is the analytic derivative; safe_hypot's scale, which is under stop_gradient; the two genuine elementwise min/max in get_delta's Gromov-product scan; and the two floors on non-differentiated paths (uniform-Poincaré direction sampling, Busemann weight-norm init). Two behavioural differences, both improvements, both from the fact that a where's VJP is a select rather than a multiply by a 0/1 factor: (1) _compute_mlr's NaN behaviour reverts — the where landed in the previous entry used the > direction, which floored a NaN z; it now uses floor_at, i.e. <, restoring the NaN propagation the original .clip(min=…) had. (2) A saturated sinh/cosh/tanh argument no longer leaks 0 * inf = NaN into a squared downstream gradient: grad((sinh∘clip)(x)²) past the overflow clamp was NaN in both dtypes and is now exactly 0. That is what test_smooth_clamp_vs_clip.py::test_saturated_tail_gradient_is_degenerate_for_both_clamps pins as a negative property, and its own docstring says to re-baseline it if it ever improves — it now needs that re-baseline (two assertions, both dtypes). Bit-identity was verified on CPU against the parent commit over 13 144 forward and gradient blob comparisons on 3 286 cases — every public method of Poincare, Hyperboloid, Euclidean, ProperVelocity, Stereographic and ProductManifold, both MLR helpers, the isometry maps, the hyperboloid_core/busemann_core functional cores and HypRegressionPoincare, over near-origin, ordinary and near-boundary/large-radius inputs plus exact-zero, exact-MIN_NORM, exact-±1, NaN and ±inf rows
  • Both hyperbolic MLR heads returned an all-NaN gradient — for the whole kernel, not just the affected class — as soon as one hyperplane normal was exactly zero. manifolds/hyperboloid._compute_mlr and nn_layers/poincare_regression.HypRegressionPoincare._compute_mlr divide by the Euclidean norm of the per-class normal and floor that norm. The floor keeps the forward value finite, but jnp.linalg.norm's VJP at the zero vector is z/‖z‖ = 0/0 = NaN, created inside the norm's own VJP — where the floor's zero cotangent meets it as 0 * NaN = NaN, so the NaN spreads to every row of the kernel gradient. An exactly-zero normal is an ordinary input (a dead or pruned output channel, or a zero-initialised head), and it was silently fatal: measured NaN in all 8 combinations of {hyperboloid MLR, Poincaré regression} × {float32, float64} × {eager, jitted}. Both now use the library's safe_norm, whose double-where gives an exact 0 value and an exactly-zero VJP at the zero vector; the floor_at guard stays in front of the division. After the fix all 8 are finite, the Poincaré head's dead row gets an exactly-zero gradient, and the hyperboloid head's dead row is inert at the min_enorm scale (max |g| 1.8e-15 float32 / 3.0e-15 float64 against ~10 for the live rows — the residual is the genuine d⟨x_s, z⟩ path, not the norm). This is the one change in this release that is not bit-identical for ordinary inputs: safe_norm is max-scaled (it divides by max|v| before squaring, which is what makes it overflow-free past ‖z‖ = 1.8e19 in float32), so the norm itself moves. Measured against a float64 reference over 20 000 vectors per cell, dims 2/8/64 and scales 1e-8/1/1e3: the norm moves by at most 2–4 ulp, and safe_norm's own error is at most ~1 ulp worse than linalg.norm's on in-range inputs (float32 max 3.2 vs 2.5 ulp, mean 0.48 vs 0.42). Downstream the alpha = -x₀·sinh(√c·r)·‖z‖ + cosh(√c·r)·⟨x_s, z⟩ cancellation amplifies that, so the MLR forward and gradient move by up to 3.6e-7 relative to each array's own scale in float32 (≈3 ulp of scale) and 6.1e-16 in float64. Accuracy is unchanged: float32-vs-float64 relative error of the forward and of grad(Σ res²) is the same before and after to within noise across c ∈ {0.3, 1} × spatial scale ∈ {1e-8, 0.5, 8} (forward 1.5e-7…2.5e-7 both; the pre-existing 1.1e-1 float32 blow-up at c = 1, radius 8 is present in both and is a separate large-radius limitation). A bit-identical alternative exists — wrapping jnp.linalg.norm in the same double-where by hand — and was not taken, because safe_norm is the library's own primitive for exactly this and additionally removes the sum(z²) overflow at large radius
  • Pairwise hyperboloid dist/sqdist/logmap lost eps·x₀ in the radial term of their polar decomposition, an O(eps/r) relative error near the origin; the gap is now built from the spatial radii. _polar_frame needs P = sinh((a−b)/2) = ½·(u_x − u_y)/(√u_x·√u_y) with u = x₀ + ‖x_s‖. Forming u_x − u_y directly subtracts two numbers of size x₀ ≈ 1/√c to obtain a difference of size ‖x_s‖ − ‖y_s‖, and x₀ is only stored to eps·x₀, so near the origin the difference is mostly rounding. It is now evaluated through the on-sheet identity x₀ − y₀ = (r_x² − r_y²)/(x₀ + y₀), i.e. u_x − u_y = (r_x − r_y)·(1 + (r_x + r_y)/(x₀ + y₀)) with r = ‖x_s‖: only the spatial radii enter the subtraction (exact by Sterbenz when they are close) and the bracket is a ratio of sums of positive numbers running from 1 at the origin to 2 at large radius, so it can neither cancel nor overflow. u_x, u_y still supply the √u_x·√u_y denominator and the isfinite guard that returns ±inf past the representable radius, so behavior there is unchanged. Relative error against a 250-digit Decimal reference evaluated on the dtype-rounded spatial parts, worst over c ∈ {0.3, 1, 2.5} and dim ∈ {8, 32}, median (max), before → after (logs/2026-09-03_polar_frame_gap/probe_polar_gap_accuracy.py, CPU backend, jax 0.9.1; the A100 agrees in every cell to within float32 rounding noise — its worst new-column value on the origin grid is 2.7e-7 against 3.1e-7 on CPU) — float32 dist(origin, x): 1.0 (1.0) → 1.8e-7 (2.8e-7) at spatial radius 1e-8, 4.6e-2 → 1.9e-8 (1.3e-7) at 1e-6, 1.4e-4 → 9.5e-8 (2.4e-7) at 1e-4, 3.1e-5 → 2.4e-7 (2.6e-7) at 1e-3, 9.7e-6 → 1.7e-7 (2.6e-7) at 1e-2, 9.7e-7 → 1.5e-7 at 0.1; float32 dist(x, y) for two points at geodesic radius 1e-3 separated by 1e-3: 3.0e-5 → 1.7e-7, at radius 0.1 separated by 1e-3: 2.0e-5 → 1.5e-6; float64 at radius 1e-3 separated by 1e-5: 1.3e-12 → 3.2e-15. No cell at large radius regresses: over the whole (geodesic radius 1 … 40) x (separation 1e-4·r … 10·r) grid every cell that gets worse does so within ulp noise — worst new/old median ratio 1.6 on a CPU float64 cell whose median relative error is 2.7e-15, 3.0 on a GPU float64 cell that moves from 1 to 3 ulp (1.1e-16 → 3.3e-16), 1.3 on a float32 cell at 1.1e-7 — plus one float32 cell sitting at 2e-4 where both arms are input-resolution-limited (ratio 1.1 CPU, 0.7 GPU); every cell at radius ≥ 10 (float32) / ≥ 20 (float64) reproduces the old median and max unchanged. dist(x, y) == dist(y, x) stays exact to the bit: r_x + r_y and x₀ + y₀ are unchanged under the swap and r_y − r_x is the exact negation of r_x − r_y. Consumers: dist, sqdist, logmap (its cos φ reads P/S from the same frame), and tangent_norm via logmap. Supersedes the sentence in the dist_0/logmap_0 entry above that calls this "a planned separate change" and advises dist_0 over dist(origin, x) — the two now agree to 3.1e-7 in float32 at every radius, though dist_0 remains marginally tighter because the MIN_NORM floor on ‖y_s‖ at the origin leaves a ½·MIN_NORM/‖x_s‖ relative residual in the pairwise arm (5e-12 at radius 1e-4, invisible in float32)
  • Poincare.dist_0(..., version_idx=2) (VERSION_METRIC_TENSOR) was floored to exactly zero for every float32 radius below ~1.1e-3/√c and every radius below 2.2e-8/√c in both dtypes; it now uses the algebraically identical arcsinh half-angle form. The arm evaluated acosh(1 + 2c‖x‖²/(1 − c‖x‖²))/√c, the same defect class as the hyperboloid's old acosh(√c·x₀) route: the entire radial signal sits in a perturbation of a leading 1, so math_utils.acosh's 1 + 10·eps domain clamp flattened everything below sqrt(10·eps/c) onto zero, and an extra arg < 1 + MIN_NORM short-circuit zeroed a second band below sqrt(MIN_NORM/2c). The identity acosh(1 + 2t) = 2·arcsinh(√t) moves the radius into an argument linear in r: with t = c‖x‖²/(1 − c‖x‖²) the arm is 2·arcsinh(√c‖x‖/sqrt(1 − c‖x‖²))/√c, which needs no domain clamp at all. Median relative error vs a 60-digit decimal reference, dim 8, before → after (CPU jax 0.9.1; the A100 agrees), float32: r=1e-8 7.7e4 → 1.4e-8, 1e-6 7.7e2 → 1.4e-8, 1e-4 6.7 → 2.9e-8, 1e-3 6.6e-3 → 5.3e-8, 1e-2 3.3e-5 → 8.6e-8, 0.1 4.9e-7 → 3.4e-8, 0.9/√c 6.5e-8 → 3.5e-8 (all at c = 1; c = 0.3 and 2.5 differ only in the floored magnitude, up to 1.4e5 at r=1e-8); float64: 1e-8 1.0 → 1.7e-16, 1e-6 1.1e-5 → 0, 1e-4 2.5e-9 → 1.4e-16, 1e-3 2.8e-12 → 0, 1e-2 1.4e-13 → 0, 0.1 2.2e-15 → 0. The jax.grad magnitude in the floored band was exactly 0 instead of the analytic 2 (float32 r ≤ 1e-6 at every curvature, r ≤ 1e-3 at c = 0.3; float64 r ≤ 1e-8), so a parameter optimised through slot 2 near the origin received no gradient at all. Not a new version slot: slot 2 is the metric-tensor distance and it is the same function, now computed accurately. The boundary guard is untouched — 1 − c‖x‖² still comes from the clamped conformal factor, so the representable ceiling stays 12.1/√c (float32) / 27.8/√c (float64) — and safe_norm supplies the exactly-zero value and VJP at the origin, so d₀(0) = 0 and jax.grad there are both unchanged (logs/2026-09-03_poincare_origin_numerics/probe_item1_metric_tensor_dist_0.py). Slots 0 and 1 were never affected
  • The pairwise Poincare.dist(..., version_idx=2) (VERSION_METRIC_TENSOR) had the same floor as its dist_0 twin: two points closer than ~1.2e-3/√c in float32 came back at exactly 0 distance with an exactly-zero gradient. The arm evaluated acosh(1 + 2t)/√c with t = c‖x - y‖²/((1 - c‖x‖²)(1 - c‖y‖²)), so math_utils.acosh's 1 + 10·eps domain clamp flattened every pair with t < 5·eps onto zero and an arg < 1 + MIN_NORM short-circuit zeroed a second band below t = MIN_NORM/2. The two (1 - c·r²) factors scale the threshold with the pair's radius: at c = 1 the float32 separation floor is 1.2e-3 at the origin and 9.2e-4 at radius 0.5. It is now the identical half-angle form 2·arcsinh(√t)/√c, √t = √c‖x - y‖/sqrt((1 - c‖x‖²)(1 - c‖y‖²)), whose argument is linear in the separation. Median relative error vs a 60-digit decimal reference routed through Möbius addition (independent of the formula under test), dim 8, c = 1, before → after — float32 at radius 1e-2: separation 1e-8 7.7e4 → 3.0e-8, 1e-6 7.7e2 → 2.6e-8, 1e-4 6.7 → 2.3e-8, 1e-2 6.7e-5 → 1.0e-7; at radius 0.5: 1e-8 3.5e4 → 3.6e-8, 1e-6 5.8e2 → 3.3e-8, 1e-4 4.8 → 4.5e-8, 1e-2 2.6e-6 → 6.1e-8. float64 at radius 1e-2: 1e-8 1.0 → 1.7e-16, 1e-6 5.4e-8 → 2.1e-16, 1e-4 2.5e-9 → 6.8e-17, 1e-2 1.9e-13 → 0; at radius 0.5: 1e-8 1.0 → 1.2e-16, 1e-6 6.3e-6 → 0, 1e-4 3.6e-10 → 0. At c = 0.3 and 2.5 only the floored magnitude differs (up to 1.4e5). 23 of 60 probed gradient cells returned an exactly-zero gradient and now return the analytic λ(y) = 2/(1 - c‖y‖²) — a loss pulling two nearby points apart through slot 2 received no gradient at all. safe_norm on x - y keeps dist(x, x) exactly 0 with a finite (zero) gradient, which is what the removed where-guard used to provide (test_precision.py::test_poincare_dist_grad_at_coincident_points). Both boundary guards are unchanged — the two 1 - c‖·‖² factors still come from the clamped conformal factors — and this is not a new version slot: slot 2 is the metric-tensor distance and it is the same function, now computed accurately (logs/2026-09-03_poincare_origin_numerics/probe_item5_metric_tensor_dist_pairwise.py). Slots 0 and 1 were never affected
  • Hyperboloid.logmap_0 returned an all-NaN vector for a point with an infinite spatial entry, wiping out the time slot too; it now returns ±inf on the infinite entries. safe_norm deliberately passes an inf through as inf so an out-of-range point stays visibly degenerate, which made u = √c·‖y_s‖ = inf and the scale arcsinh(u)/u an inf/inf NaN that then multiplied every spatial entry. The pairwise dist / _polar_frame convention for an out-of-range input is ±inf, not NaN, and logmap_0 now matches it: scale = where(isfinite(u), arcsinh(u)/u, 1), so an infinite entry comes back as ±inf with its sign, the finite entries keep their own values, and the time slot stays exactly 0 — the right limit, since the tangent vector toward an infinitely far point has infinite norm and its direction is the unit vector along the infinite coordinate. NaN in still gives NaN out, but only in the NaN entry rather than across the whole vector. The guard is a where on the scalar u, so the finite path is unchanged. Over 2000 log-spaced spatial magnitudes 1e-20…1e10 in both dtypes the forward value is bit-identical on both backends (0 of 18000 bit patterns), and the gradient is bit-identical on XLA:CPU; on XLA:GPU the gradient moves by at most 2 ulps on 614 (float32) / 626 (float64) of 18000 entries, because the extra where changes how XLA:GPU fuses the VJP. That is below the 4-ulp spread the unchanged code already shows between the two backends (4294 of 18000 float32 gradient entries differ CPU-vs-GPU before the change), and each backend is deterministic run to run (logs/2026-09-03_poincare_origin_numerics/probe_item2_logmap_0_inf.py)
  • Every additive-epsilon norm in the library is gone: sqrt(sum(x**2) + MIN_NORM**2) overflowed float32 above coordinate 1.8e19 and floored every genuinely small vector at 1e-15. The idiom was a gradient guard — it gives sqrt a finite derivative at x = 0, which jnp.linalg.norm does not (its VJP there is 0/0 = NaN) — and it paid for that at both ends of the exponent range. Overflow: Hyperboloid.proj at float32 spatial radius 5e19 returned x0 = inf, and already at 1e19 its Minkowski residual -x0² + ‖x_s‖² evaluated to exactly 0 instead of -1/c; expmap_0 inherited both through its trailing _proj. The Poincaré ball's boundary clamp failed the same way but louder: with ‖x‖ = inf the clamp x·(max_norm/‖x‖) is the zero vector, so a float32 point at radius 1e20 was projected onto the origin rather than onto the boundary (measured ‖proj(x)‖ = 0.0; it is now 0.99999). pv_to_poincare and pv_to_hyperboloid had the same ceiling on dot(x, x). Underflow: the +MIN_NORM² = 1e-30 floor dominates any genuinely small vector, relative residual MIN_NORM²/(2r²) — Poincare.dist_0 of a float32 point at radius 1e-15 returned 2.83e-15 for a true 2.00e-15 (41 % high, and every smaller radius collapsed onto that same value), and a float64 point at radius 1e-8 was 5.0e-15 high. 59 sites across manifolds/, nn_layers/ and distributions/ now use safe_norm / safe_hypot / the new safe_sqrt — 47 here and 12 more on the hot path, split into their own commit so the kernel cost can be reverted independently — and no occurrence of the old idiom is left in the package. 36 floors that bound a value rather than a derivative (Minkowski forms, conformal factors, explicit divisor guards, BatchNorm and Adam epsilons) are deliberate and unchanged, each with its reason in logs/2026-09-03_safe_norm_sweep/inventory.md. One consequence had to be undone: the old idiom's sqrt(jnp.sum(x**2) + eps) reduces every axis, so on the (B, dim) arrays several call sites hand these single-point ops it produced a scalar that broadcast (against the whole batch, i.e. a Frobenius norm — silently not a per-row one), while safe_norm reduces only the last axis and the (B,) result no longer broadcasts at all; 14 norms that scale a (..., dim) operand get the trailing axis back as [..., None] (_gyrovector_core._proj, Poincare._expmap/_expmap_0, six Stereographic maps plus _geodesic_unit/_antipode, and ProperVelocity._scalar_mul/_expmap_0/_logmap_0/_logmap), and Poincare._scalar_mul/_logmap_0 take axis=-1, keepdims=True on their whole-array jnp.sum for the same reason. Bit-identical on the single-point contract (8100 evaluations across 5 manifolds × 15 ops × 2 dtypes × dims 2/5/12 × 3 curvatures × 6 seeds — 0 value and 0 shape differences) and free (A100 kernel/reduction counts unchanged on all five probed ops); on a batched input every one of them is now exactly the per-row result, which tests/test_class_based_manifolds.py::test_implicitly_batched_call_equals_the_per_row_call pins. A second consequence is now gone too, and it cost accuracy rather than shapes: the rescaling divided by max|v| itself, which is an inexact division, so the result carried 1–2 ulp that the old sqrt(sum(v**2) + eps) did not — visible wherever a caller recomputes the same sum of squares, as the hyperboloid does (x₀ = sqrt(‖x_s‖² + 1/c) checked against -x₀² + ‖x_s‖² = -1/c, where at x₀ ≈ 34 in float32 one ulp of x₀² is 1.2e-4, larger than the 1e-4 tolerance the HRC norm layers are checked at). The divisor is now the exact power of two just below max|v| (jnp.frexp/jnp.ldexp), which shifts the exponent and nothing else, so it contributes no rounding of its own: over magnitudes 1e-15…1e15 (float32) and 1e-30…1e30 (float64), dims 2/4/16/64, safe_norm matches a jitted sqrt(sum(v**2)) on all but 1 of 480 000 values, against 67 239 of 160 000 for the divide-by-max form. Bit-identity is not unconditional and is not claimed to be: which association XLA gives a last-axis reduction depends on the surrounding fusion, and at dim 8 the two programs happen to differ by 1–2 ulp (mean 0.13–0.17) where at dims 2/4/16/64 they agree exactly — the divide-by-max form is 1–3 ulp with mean 0.34–0.62 at every dim. The overflow-free property is untouched (a float32 vector at radius 1e20 still returns 2.83e20, not inf). The other half of the accuracy loss was the shape of the two-leg reconstruction: safe_hypot(safe_norm(v), q) rounds ‖v‖ and squares it again, which is up to one ulp of sum(v**2) and cannot cancel. A new hyperbolix.utils.safe_hypot_norm(v, q) computes sqrt(‖v‖² + q²) in one reduction, reproducing the association of the sqrt(sum(v**2) + q**2) it replaces, and the nine sites that reconstruct a hyperboloid time slot or an epsilon-floored norm use it (Hyperboloid._proj/_proj_batch, isometry_mappings.pv_to_hyperboloid, hyperboloid_core.spatial_to_hyperboloid/build_spacelike_V, both hyperboloid_linear reconstructions, both hyperboloid_attention norms). The Minkowski residual of HRCBatchNorm/HRCRMSNorm at c_in = 10 -> c_out = 0.1 goes 6.1e-5/3.1e-5 (pre-sweep) -> 1.5e-4/1.2e-4 (sweep, both over the 1e-4 tolerance) -> 6.1e-5/6.1e-5. All 11 probed A100 ops are unchanged in kernels and reductions, so both halves are free. The three sqrt(1 + c‖x‖²) sites — ProperVelocity._beta_inv, its _compute_mlr twin and isometry_mappings.pv_to_poincare — are converted too, as safe_hypot_norm(√c·x, 1). Measured against an 80-bit longdouble reference over c ∈ {0.3, 1, 2.5}, dims 2/8/16, both dtypes and radii 1e-3…1e3, that is the most accurate of the three overflow-free spellings: mean 0.25 ulp / max 2 and exact on 75.0 % of values, against 0.32 / max 3 / 69.5 % for the two-leg safe_hypot(1, √c·safe_norm(x)) it replaces and 0.30 / max 3 / 70.8 % for the variant that scales the scalar leg (√c·safe_hypot_norm(x, 1/√c), exact at c = 1 but 0.45 ulp at c = 2.5 in float64, where 1/√c is itself inexact). Scaling the components cannot overflow where the result does not, since 1/β_x ≥ √c·‖x‖ ≥ √c·max|xᵢ|: at float32 radius 1e20, _beta_inv is 1.55e20/2.83e20/4.47e20 at those three curvatures and pv_to_poincare lands the point exactly on the ball boundary 1/√c, with a finite (zero) gradient at the origin
  • Four norms had no guard at all and returned a NaN gradient at the zero vector: Euclidean.dist, Euclidean.dist_0, Euclidean.tangent_norm and ProperVelocity.tangent_norm, plus all three ProductManifold methods that call them. The first three were bare jnp.linalg.norm, whose VJP at the zero vector is 0/0 = NaN; ProperVelocity.tangent_norm and ProductManifold.tangent_norm were sqrt(floor_at(g_x(v,v), 0.0)), where sqrt'(0) = inf meets a zero cotangent as 0·inf = NaN. Measured on the parent (logs/2026-09-03_safe_norm_sweep/parent_gate/gate.py): grad(Euclidean.dist_0)(0), grad(Euclidean.dist)(x, x), grad(ProperVelocity.tangent_norm)(0) and ProductManifold.dist_0 / dist / tangent_norm at the product origin all returned all-NaN (the product cases NaN only in the Euclidean factor's slots, poisoning the sum). All six now return exactly zero — the finite, direction-free choice where the derivative does not exist. Reachable from any model with a Euclidean factor in a product manifold, or any Riemannian-norm regulariser evaluated at a dead unit

  • A new hyperbolix.utils.math_utils.safe_sqrt, the scalar counterpart of safe_norm: sqrt(x) with the same double-where, so the derivative at x == 0 is exactly 0 rather than inf. For the quantities that arrive already squared — Minkowski and Riemannian forms g_x(v, v), sums of per-factor squared distances — which safe_norm cannot take (its input is the vector, and a Minkowski form is not a Euclidean norm). Exported from hyperbolix.utils

  • Hyperboloid.proj returned an infinite time coordinate for any float32 point past spatial radius 1.8e19, and a Minkowski residual of exactly 0 instead of -1/c just below it. x₀ = sqrt(floor_at(1/c + dot(x_s, x_s), MIN_NORM)) forms the sum of squares, which overflows float32 as soon as a spatial coordinate passes 1.8e19 — while ‖x_s‖ itself, and therefore x₀, is a perfectly ordinary float. Measured on the parent at c = 1 (logs/2026-09-03_safe_norm_sweep/parent_gate/gate.py): radius 5e19 and 1e20 give x₀ = inf; radius 1e19 gives a finite x₀ = 1e19 whose constraint -x₀² + ‖x_s‖² evaluates to 0.0 rather than -1.0, because sqrt of the (still finite) sum has lost the 1/c entirely. expmap_0 inherited both through its trailing _proj — a tangent vector of length 1e19 came back as [inf, 7.0e37, 0, 0]. It is now the two-leg safe_hypot(1/√c, safe_norm(x_s)), which never materialises ‖x_s‖²: the constraint holds to 1e-6 relative (checked in float64 against the float32 output) at every radius from 1e19 to 1e20, in proj, proj_batch and expmap_0. Dropping the MIN_NORM floor is a no-op on the finite domain — 1/c + ‖x_s‖² ≥ 1/c > 1e-15 for every curvature below 1e15 — and lets a non-finite input pass through as inf, the convention safe_norm and the pairwise dist already follow. nn_layers carried three copies of the same sqrt(‖z‖² + 1/c) reconstruction (_fhcnn_forward, _fgg_linear_forward, hyperboloid_core.spatial_to_hyperboloid) and isometry_mappings.pv_to_hyperboloid a fourth; all four are converted

  • The Poincaré ball's boundary clamp projected the farthest representable point onto the origin. _gyrovector_core._proj computes where(‖x‖ > max_norm, x·(max_norm/‖x‖), x) with the same overflowing sqrt(sum(x**2) + MIN_NORM**2). Past float32 coordinate 1.8e19 that norm is inf, so the scale factor is max_norm/inf = 0 and the clamp returns the zero vector — the point farthest from where it belongs. Measured on the parent: ‖proj(x)‖ = 0.0 at radius 1e20 (it is 0.99999, i.e. max_norm, at 1e19, where the norm has not yet overflowed). It is now floor_at(safe_norm(x), MIN_NORM): the floor stays, because norm divides in the untaken branch of the where as well and a zero cotangent against that branch's inf is NaN. _proj_batch had the same defect and the same fix
  • ProperVelocity._beta collapsed to 0 for any point past ‖x‖ = 1.8e19/√c. 1/sqrt(1 + c·dot(x, x)) overflows the same way, and _beta is the coefficient every PV gyro-operation is built from — _addition, _expmap, _logmap, _dpi_x, _tangent_inner — so one overflowing coordinate silently zeroed all of them. ‖x‖ = 1.8e19 is geodesic radius arcsinh(1.8e19) ≈ 44, well inside the range PV exists to serve: it is the unconstrained model, chosen precisely because it stays stable where the ball saturates. _beta_inv is now safe_hypot(1, √c·safe_norm(x)) and _beta its reciprocal; isometry_mappings.pv_to_poincare had the same expression and the same fix (there the overflow mapped a far-out PV point to the ball origin)
  • The FHNN linear/conv forward returned an all-inf spatial row for any float32 time coordinate past y0 = 1.844e19. _fhnn_forward recovered the target spatial norm from the hyperboloid constraint as sqrt(y0**2 - 1/c), and y0**2 overflows float32 at sqrt(FLT_MAX) = 1.844e19 — a regime capped_exp deliberately allows y0 to reach, since it caps a runaway scale at exp(0.99·log(FLT_MAX)) ≈ 6.1e37 precisely so the value stays finite. Measured on the parent (logs/2026-09-04_flags_batch/probe_diff_of_squares.py, c = 1): y0 = 1e20 gives [1.0e20, inf, -inf, inf] and d‖y_s‖/dy0 = 0 instead of 1. It is now the factored difference of squares sqrt(y0 - 1/√c) · sqrt(y0 + 1/√c), whose two factors are each strictly positive because y0 > 1/√c + eps holds by construction (additive floor, not a max): finite through y0 = 3e38, with ‖y_s‖/y0 → 1 to 1e-6 relative and finite gradients. This is the difference-of-squares counterpart of the safe_hypot sum-of-squares conversion above, and it was the one remaining site of its kind in the library. Values are not bit-identical in float32. Over a margin-stratified grid (y0 - 1/√c from 1e-2 to 1e19, c in {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5}, logs/2026-09-04_flags_batch/probe_ordinary_range.py) the two forms differ by at most 3.1e-6 relative, at the smallest margins; above margin 1 it is 1-2 ulps. Where they disagree materially the factored form is the more accurate of the two against a float64 reference (worst case 1.3e-6 vs the old form's 2.9e-6 at margin ≤ 1); in the large-margin bands the old form is exact and the new one carries 1 ulp

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The hot-path half of the norm conversion (proj, proj_batch, expmap_0, logmap_0 on every manifold, plus the Proper-Velocity _beta/_beta_inv/_safe_norm helpers) is a separate commit, and it costs one XLA kernel. Compile-only counts for jax.jit(jax.vmap(op)) at batch 1e7, dim 32, float32 on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, logs/2026-09-03_safe_norm_sweep/probe_xla_kernels.py, kernels/reductions, before -> after): Poincaré expmap_0 3/1 -> 5/2 and proj 3/1 -> 5/2; hyperboloid proj 1/1 -> 2/2, expmap_0 2/2 -> 3/3, and addition 7/8 -> 9/9 (it calls proj). Unchanged: Poincaré dist 2/4, logmap_0 3/1, mobius_add 3/5, ptransp 3/5, and hyperboloid logmap_0 3/2, dist 6/6. The extra reduction is the max|x| that max-scaling needs, and it is unavoidable here: these are exactly the sites whose input is by definition unprojected, so the overflow they fix is reachable and the cheap safe_sqrt spelling used elsewhere would not fix it. Reverting this commit alone restores the old kernel counts and leaves the other 47 conversions in place.

  • The additive-epsilon norm replacement moves float32 values by 1-3 ulps and is free on GPU. Which primitive replaces which site is a cost decision: safe_norm's max-scaling costs a second reduction over the input, so it is used only where the input magnitude is genuinely unbounded (tangent vectors, unprojected points, hyperboloid/PV coordinates, layer weights). Where the argument is a ball point — Poincare.dist, dist_0, logmap, scalar_mul, the Apollonian metric — sum(x**2) <= 4/c and overflow is unreachable, so those use safe_sqrt(sum(x**2)), the same double-where on the scalar. Compile-only kernel counts for jax.jit(jax.vmap(op)) at batch 1e7, dim 32, float32 on an A100 (jax 0.9.1, logs/2026-09-03_safe_norm_sweep/probe_xla_kernels.py): every one of the 11 probed ops is unchanged in both kernels and reductions — Poincaré dist 2/4, expmap_0 3/1, logmap_0 3/1, mobius_add 3/5, ptransp 3/5, proj 3/1; hyperboloid proj 1/1, expmap_0 2/2, logmap_0 3/2, dist 6/6, addition 7/8. (Spelling Poincare.dist's numerator safe_norm instead would have cost it 2 -> 4 kernels and 4 -> 5 reductions for an overflow that cannot happen there; that measurement is in the same log directory.) One subtlety the conversion has to respect: where a floored norm feeds a sinh(t)/t, the floor belongs on t itself and not only on the denominator, or the ratio is 0 instead of 1 at t = 0

  • The pairwise dist gap term reads x₀ only through a well-conditioned sum, so the spatial part is now the source of truth for the radial split too. For an input that is off the sheet, dist/sqdist/logmap now report the gap implied by its spatial radii — the same convention proj (which rebuilds x₀ from x_s), dist_0 and logmap_0 already follow — rather than one read off an x₀ inconsistent with them. On-sheet inputs are unaffected beyond the accuracy change above. A raw jax.grad(dist) correspondingly moves its radial support from the time slot to the spatial slot; the two gradients differ by a multiple of the constraint normal, so after egrad2rgrad/tangent_proj the Riemannian gradient is unchanged and the Riemannian optimizers are unaffected. Measured over 75 (curvature x radius x radius) cells, CPU and A100 alike (logs/2026-09-03_polar_frame_gap/probe_polar_gap_gradient.py): worst old-vs-new relative disagreement 3.6e-14 (float64) and 4.3e-7 median / 3.7e-5 worst (float32); in the three float32 cells above 1e-5 the old arm is the one that moved — against the same pair promoted to float64 the new gradient is within 1.1e-6 while the old carries the full 3.7e-5
  • Breaking: dist_0(..., version_idx=2) and version_idx=3 now return the pre-fix acosh arms. Those two slots used to duplicate slots 0 and 1 for the origin distance; they now select VERSION_LEGACY / VERSION_LEGACY_SMOOTHENED, mirroring what they have meant for the pairwise dist since 1.1.2, and exist only to reproduce results computed before this fix. Code that passed 2 or 3 to dist_0 and expected default behavior must pass VERSION_DEFAULT (0) or VERSION_SMOOTHENED (1)
  • dist_0 and logmap_0 read the radius off x_s and ignore x₀. An off-sheet input therefore gets the radius of its proj projection, which is the convention proj itself follows (it rebuilds x₀ from x_s) and what ProperVelocity.dist_0 already did. A raw jax.grad(dist_0) consequently has its support on x_s instead of on x₀; the two gradients differ by a multiple of the constraint normal, so after egrad2rgrad/tangent_proj the Riemannian gradient is identical and the Riemannian optimizers are unaffected
  • Poincare.expmap_0 clamps the boundary on the scalar instead of re-projecting its output. It now computes t = min(tanh(√c·‖v‖), √c·max_norm) and res = t/(√c·‖v‖) · v, so ‖res‖ ≤ max_norm holds by construction and the trailing proj (a second norm reduction over the op's own output) is gone. Under jax.jit(jax.vmap(...)) at batch 1e7, dim 32 the op compiles to 3 kernels with 1 reduction instead of 5 with 2 (logs/2026-09-02_submission-numerics/probe_xla_kernels.py, A100, jax 0.9.1 and 0.11.0). Values move only on rows the projection clamps (‖v‖ ≳ 8/√c in float32): at most 3.4e-7 relative (float32, c ≤ 5) / 6.0e-16 (float64), overshooting max_norm by at most 2.2 eps, 50x inside the eps**0.75 margin; Jacobians agree on unclamped rows. _gyrovector_core._max_norm is the factored bound; proj itself is unchanged bit-for-bit.
  • Möbius addition x ⊕ y computes its own output norm from reductions over the inputs, so the boundary clamp is a scalar comparison instead of a second pass over the result. _gyrovector_core._addition used to build num = A·x + B·y (A = 1 + 2c⟨x,y⟩ + c‖y‖², B = 1 − c‖x‖²) and call proj(num/denom, c), which reduces ‖·‖ over the op's own (dim,) output. It now regroups the numerator as num = B·(x+y) + c‖x+y‖²·x — identical in exact arithmetic, since A − B = c‖x+y‖² — and expands ‖num‖² = B²·s2 + 2·B·(c·s2)·⟨x,s⟩ + (c·s2)²·‖x‖² with s = x+y, s2 = ‖s‖², in the same two coefficients that built num. Five input reductions (‖x‖², ‖y‖², ⟨x,y⟩, s2, ⟨x,s⟩) replace three plus one output reduction. Under jax.jit(jax.vmap(...)) at batch 1e7, dim 32, float32 the op compiles to 3 kernels / 5 reductions / 5 (B, dim)-sized memory passes, from 5 / 4 / 7 — XLA folds all five reductions into a single multi-output kInput fusion and the unprojected (B, dim) intermediate, which previously had to be written and read back, is gone (logs/2026-09-02_submission-numerics/probe_xla_kernels.py, A100, jax 0.9.1; dist stays 2 / 4 and expmap_0 3 / 1). H100 timing pending — run logs/2026-09-02_submission-numerics/probe_gpu_timing.py. The regrouping is what makes the analytic norm safe, and it is not interchangeable with the textbook ‖num‖² = A²‖x‖² + 2AB⟨x,y⟩ + B²‖y‖². Take x near the boundary, ε := 1 − c‖x‖², and y = −x + n: A·x and B·y are each of size ε‖x‖ but their sum is O(ε²), so every norm derived from A and B is a difference of terms 1/ε² larger than its own value, and the floating-point vector fl(A·x) + fl(B·y) itself differs from the exact A·x + B·y by a relative eps/ε — which means the clamp can scale a row to sit outside the ball even when the norm formula has no cancellation of its own. B·(x+y) and c‖x+y‖²·x are individually the same order as their sum (cancelling only in the collinear case, and there by at most a factor 2 for a y inside the ball), which is why this grouping keeps norm and vector consistent. Measured on 2.7M adversarial rows per dtype — random pairs, x ⊕ (−x), coincident points, and a near-boundary antipodal grid spanning ε ∈ {1e-2 … the eps**0.75 ceiling margin} × ‖n‖/(εR) ∈ {0.01 … 10} × three directions of n, at c ∈ {0.3, 1, 2.5} (logs/2026-09-03_b2_mobius_norm/probe_mobius_norm.py): worst overshoot of max_norm is 10 ulps and no row exceeds max_norm·(1 + 16·eps), leaving the result inside the true radius 1/√c with 54x (float32) / 26000x (float64) of the eps**0.75 margin to spare. The three-dot form overshoots by up to 3.5e5 ulps and the (A+B)/2, (A−B)/2 form — cancellation-free as a formula, but a norm of the exact A·x + B·y — by up to 6.5e9; both put 9% of the antipodal rows more than 1% outside the ball. Zero NaN or inf in values or in grad(Σ dist) / grad(Σ logmap) on every family. Values are not bit-identical to the previous release. On well-conditioned inputs rows move by at most 5.7e-7 (float32) / 1.5e-15 (float64) of the ball radius, i.e. 2–3 ulps, and the clamp decision differs on ≤ 1.3e-4 of rows. Where the two forms disagree materially the new one is more accurate: against a float64 reference its error is 0.48–0.60x the old form's at every ε in the antipodal grid; x ⊕ (−x) is now exactly zero, where the old form left a residue of up to 1.3e-3 of the ball radius in float32; and at the float64 ceiling margin (ε ≈ 4e-12) the error is ~1e-7 of the radius against the old form's 1.0, i.e. the old numerator there was pure rounding noise. On the near-boundary antipodal grid the clamp decisions differ on 20–70% of rows, which is expected and not a regression: that is the regime in which the old implementation's own decision was made on a numerator with no significant bits left. proj and proj_batch are untouched, and every other caller of them is unaffected.
  • Float32 tanh and atanh in hyperbolix.utils.math_utils are closer to correctly rounded (exact bit-pattern ulps vs a float64 reference, 20k inputs per range, max ulp before → after). atanh below 1/8 uses the odd Maclaurin series through x⁹ (float32 only; float64 keeps the single-log1p form bit-for-bit): GPU 3 → 1, CPU 2 → 1. tanh for |x| ≥ 1/8 (float32; 1/2 in float64) uses t/(t + 2) with t = expm1(2|x|): GPU [0.125, 0.9] 4 → 3 and [0.9, 7] 5 → 2; CPU [0.9, 7] 4 → 1; float64 CPU [0.9, 7] 5 → 1. No range regresses on either backend; both wrappers stay bitwise odd with derivative exactly 1 at 0, seams are continuous to ≤ 2 ulp, and the float32 derivative's error vs 1 − tanh² drops from 1.2e-6 to 2.4e-7. Effect on the float32 Poincaré round trip logmap_0(expmap_0(v)) (dim 32, c = 1, median relative error): radius 4: 1.69e-5 → 5.4e-6 (GPU) and 5.7e-6 (CPU); radius 1e-3 on CPU 2.4e-7 → 1.2e-7; GPU at radius ≤ 1 unchanged (already at the noise floor). Below 1/8 tanh uses neither kernel: it evaluates the odd Maclaurin series x − x³/3 + 2x⁵/15 − 17x⁷/315 (Horner in x² on |x|, float32 only — float64 keeps jnp.tanh below its own 1/2 seam bit-for-bit). On [1e-4, 0.125], 20k log-uniform inputs at both signs, max / mean ulp: GPU 4 / 0.87 → 1 / 0.16, CPU 4 / 0.96 → 1 / 0.16. The series' first dropped term is 62x⁹/2835, i.e. 1.6e-10 absolute at x = 1/8 against a float32 eps of 1.2e-7, so on that range it is exact to rounding; the expm1 form cannot be used there (6 ulp on CPU). Nothing above the seam moves — [0.125, 0.9] and [0.9, 7] are bit-for-bit identical on both backends — and the float32 tanh seam gap shrinks from 0/1/0 ulp (CPU) and 2/1/2 (GPU) to 1/1/1 and 1/0/1. Poincaré round trip at radius 1e-3 (dim 32, c = 1, median relative error) drops a second time on CPU, 1.2e-7 → exactly 0, matching the GPU; radius 0.1: 1.0e-7 → 5.2e-8; radius ≥ 1 unchanged.
  • Poincare.scalar_mul and Poincare.expmap route their tanh through hyperbolix.utils.math_utils.tanh, the accurate wrapper expmap_0 already used. The two were the last raw jnp.tanh calls in the module. The wrapper is more accurate in float32 (odd Maclaurin series below |x| = 1/8, expm1 form above it, vs XLA's ~4 ulp rational approximation) and its ±(1 - 10·eps) output clip pairs with atanh's own domain guard, so an atanh/tanh round trip cannot reach the pole. Values are not bit-identical in float32. Measured over 1152 rows per op (dim 16, radii log-spaced across the whole in-ball range, c in {0.3, 1, 2.5}, r in [-2.5, 2.5]), max relative movement: scalar_mul 3.2e-7 and expmap 2.6e-7 in float32 (2-3 ulps; ~36% of entries move), and 4.2e-16 / 5.9e-16 in float64 — where movement occurs only above the wrapper's own float64 seam at |x| = 1/2; below it the wrapper falls back to XLA's tanh and every entry is bit-identical (0 of 3072 bit patterns changed) (logs/2026-09-03_poincare_origin_numerics/probe_item3_tanh_wrapper_and_proj_batch.py)
  • _gyrovector_core._proj_batch takes its boundary bound from the _max_norm helper instead of re-inlining the expression. _max_norm reads only the array's dtype, so the bound is a scalar either way and the clamp is bit-identical: 0 of 3072 bit patterns move in either dtype over a (64, 16) batch at c in {0.3, 1, 2.5} with rows inside, exactly at, and up to 1e8 past the boundary plus an exact-zero row, and _proj_batch(X, c) still equals row-wise _proj bit for bit
  • Developer tooling: undefined names are checked again. [tool.pyright] listed "hyperbolix" in both include and exclude, so pyright analysed 0 of 57 modules and always reported "0 errors"; the tree is analysed again under typeCheckingMode = "off" with reportUndefinedVariable (plus the existing unused/duplicate-import rules) enabled explicitly. Ruff's F821 is now on for tests/ and ignored only under hyperbolix/**, where jaxtyping shape strings produce 572 false positives and no true ones. New tests/test_imports.py imports every module in the package, one test per module.
  • Developer tooling: pyright runs in typeCheckingMode = "basic" and the package is clean — 0 errors, with no rule disabled and no # type: ignore added to get there. Basic mode reported 110 errors when it was first switched on (reportOperatorIssue 49, reportArgumentType 46, reportReturnType 5, 10 others). 93 of them were one thing: the Curvature union ScalarCurvature | Sequence[ScalarCurvature] was the annotation on every manifold's c, so jnp.sqrt(c), c * x and 1/c were all checked against a sequence that supports none of them. Every single manifold and the Manifold protocol itself now declare c: ScalarCurvature — 286 annotations across 19 modules — and only ProductManifold keeps the union, which still satisfies the protocol because an implementation's parameter may be wider than the one it implements. ScalarCurvature is exported from hyperbolix.manifolds alongside Curvature, and no runtime behaviour changes: this is the annotation catching up with what the code always required. Three real defects came out with it: the Manifold protocol was missing the trailing version_idx on dist/dist_0 and atol on is_in_manifold/is_in_tangent_space that its own docstring promised (so compute_pairwise_distances, which forwards version_idx, did not type-check against it); hyperbolix.utils.__all__ listed MATMUL_PRECISION, which moved to hyperbolix.utils.precision and was never re-imported, so from hyperbolix.utils import * raised AttributeError; and hyp_pad2d(pad_mode="origin") documents c as required but never checked it, failing with an opaque TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for / — it now raises a ValueError naming the argument. scalar_mul's r is widened from float to float | Float[Array, ""], which is what GyroBatchNorm/GyroRMSNorm already pass and what ProperVelocity._scalar_mul already declared. The remaining handful were values whose type @jax.jit erases: jax annotates the decorator as returning jax.stages.Wrapped, whose __call__ returns Any, so safe_norm(x) and every other jitted helper in hyperbolix.utils.math_utils handed its callers an untyped value, which pyright then widened into Array | tuple[Array, ...] at the next jnp.where and reported against whatever declared type that union eventually reached. The 13 decorators in that module now go through a one-line _jit wrapper typed Callable[P, R] -> Callable[P, R], so the declared return type survives; it returns exactly the object jax.jit returns, so tracing, the compilation cache, __name__, __doc__ and static_argnames are all unchanged.
  • API reference now covers the full hyperbolix.utils export surface and hyperbolix.utils.precision, with several stale version/count claims and numeric docstring constants corrected.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Four tests and one test oracle asserted properties no GPU backend promises, and now assert what the backend can actually deliver. None of the tolerances that guard a library defect moved. (1) XLA:GPU's float32 divide is only faithfully rounded — x / x != 1.0 for 16.25 % of 200 000 random float32 values, error up to 2 ulp (float64 is exact; CPU is exact in both). That 1-ulp perturbation of a unit direction is amplified by √(r_x·r_y) ≈ e^((a+b)/2)/(2√c) in the pairwise distance's angular term, so test_hyperboloid_dist_stable_exact_along_radial_geodesic drops its (29, 30) radius pair from the float32 leg (float64 keeps its own (19, 20) and (55, 60) pairs), and test_hyperboloid_dist_on_a_shared_ray_is_the_radius_difference caps its float32 legs at a ≤ 5. This is not a GPU-only limit: float32 cannot resolve collinearity in the ambient chart past radius ≈16 on any backend — with a generic (rather than all-components-equal) direction the same construction fails on CPU from radius 20 — so _hyperboloid_basis's docstring claim of a radius-80 threshold is corrected to the measured ≈16. (2) test_poincare_proj_batch_matches_the_vmapped_single_point_proj asserted rtol=0, atol=0 between reductions over (8, 10) and (2, 8, 10); XLA:GPU picks its reduce kernel per shape by autotuning, so the two disagreed by 1–2 ulp in 1 of 3 process launches. Now 2 ulp of the dtype. (3) test_activation_applies_euclidean_fn_to_spatial asserted bit equality between a jitted and an eager transcendental; float64 tanh differs by 1 ulp on one element in ten on GPU. Now 1 ulp — the two value assertions in that test stay strict. (4) _naive_lorentz_midpoint, the baseline test_lorentz_midpoint_small_norm_matches_naive compares the library against, carries the same MATMUL_PRECISION as the library: with the library fixed and the baseline still on TF32, that comparison measured TF32 rather than the difference between the two algebraic forms
  • Near-origin float32 accuracy depends on the backend, and the gap is XLA's transcendental kernels, not the formulas. Exact bit-pattern ulp error against a float64 reference (20k inputs in [1e-4, 0.9], max / mean): tanh 4 / 0.85 (XLA GPU), 4 / 0.90 (XLA CPU), 1 / 0.01 (torch CPU), 2 / 0.17 (torch CUDA); atanh 3 / 0.45 (XLA GPU), 2 / 0.25 (XLA CPU), 1 / 0.00 (torch CPU), 3 / 0.45 (torch CUDA, bit-identical to XLA GPU); arcsinh 2 on all four; expm1 1 (GPU) / 5 (CPU). Consequence for float32 Poincaré logmap_0(expmap_0(v)) at radius 1e-3 (dim 32, median relative error): 2.4e-7 on the CPU backend before the tanh/atanh change above (1.2e-7 with the expm1 seam, exactly 0 once the below-1/8 series landed), exactly 0 on GPU throughout. A torch-based library reaches ~1.5e-8 on CPU because torch's CPU tanh/atanh are correctly rounded; on CUDA it has no such edge. The closed forms are identical and nothing in hyperbolix is wrong here, but quote the backend alongside any near-origin float32 accuracy number
  • Poincaré round-trip ceiling. proj holds points inside 1/√c by a margin of eps**0.75 (_gyrovector_core._get_max_norm_eps), which caps the largest representable geodesic radius at atanh(1 − eps**0.75)/√c. Past it expmap_0 saturates and logmap_0(expmap_0(v)) returns the ceiling instead of v. Measured ceilings (median returned radius, in units of 1/√c): hyperbolix 6.32 (float32) / 13.86 (float64); geoopt and hypLL both 3.11 / 6.10, from fixed margins of 4e-3 and 1e-5; the unguarded closed form 8.66 / 18.72. The wider margin is deliberate, capping the conformal factor at ~3e5 (float32) / ~1e12 (float64)
  • The float64 CPU log1p hole that 1.1.1's atanh rewrite worked around is fixed upstream (openxla/xla#46765, shipped in jax ≥ 0.11.1; tracked as jax-ml/jax#39707). The rewrite stays: it costs nothing and still protects jax ≤ 0.11.0, which is what the lockfile pins (0.9.1)
  • Removed the tautological tests/test_manifolds.py::test_hyperboloid_scalar_mul_eq2. It asserted t ⊙ x == expmap_0(t · logmap_0(x)), which became a comparison of Hyperboloid.scalar_mul against its own implementation once that was rewritten to _expmap_0(r * _logmap_0(x, c), c) — the paper's Eq. 2 verbatim. The property it was meant to pin is covered non-circularly by test_hyperboloid_scalar_mul_matches_the_closed_form_near_the_origin, which checks t ⊙ x against the analytic [cosh(√c·t·d₀)/√c, sinh(√c·t·d₀)/√c · x̂_s] down to spatial radius 1e-8

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Hyperboloid dist/logmap/sqdist/tangent_norm lost all precision for two points that were each far from the origin and close together — now cancellation-free at any representable radius. Every one of these routed through the Minkowski inner product ⟨x,y⟩_L = -x₀y₀ + ⟨x_s,y_s⟩, a subtraction of two positive terms each roughly e^(√c·(d₀(x)+d₀(y))) in size; the number of significant digits lost is set by the Gromov-product-like quantity √c·(d₀(x)+d₀(y)-d(x,y)), and past ln(1/eps) — 15.9 (float32) / 36.0 (float64) — every digit of the result is cancellation noise, not signal. Measured before this fix: float32 dist returned 0.0015 for a true distance of 1.0 between two points at radius 10; logmap returned NaN from radius ~10 (float32) / ~20 (float64); tangent_norm returned ~0 (a 100% error, no warning) on exactly-unit tangent vectors past radius 8 (float32) / 20 (float64). Deep metric-learning embeddings routinely sit at radius 30–60, so this was not an edge case. dist, sqdist, and logmap are rewritten to share a _polar_frame decomposition built from the hyperbolic law of cosines in half-angle (haversine) form — a sum of non-negative terms with nothing to cancel; tangent_norm eliminates v₀ through the tangency condition, trading one power of x₀ out of the error (now exact to radius ~15 float32 / ~25 float64, up from ~8/~20). Values inside the previously-trusted regime change within the old float32/float64 noise level; values past the threshold change from silent garbage to correct. VERSION_LEGACY (2) and VERSION_LEGACY_SMOOTHENED (3) reproduce the pre-fix acosh-based arms bit-for-bit, for reproducing results computed before this fix — VERSION_DEFAULT (0) and VERSION_SMOOTHENED (1) now point at the stable forms. expmap (two-point), ptransp, tangent_proj, tangent_inner, egrad2rgrad, and is_in_manifold still route through the Minkowski inner product and remain unsafe past the same threshold; origin-chart operations (dist_0, logmap_0, expmap_0) read the radius straight off the ambient time coordinate and were never affected. New hyperbolix.utils.safe_norm/safe_hypot/safe_normalize — overflow- and underflow-free norm primitives the new decomposition depends on — are exported alongside the fix. Supersedes the VERSION_SMOOTHENED floor value (≈ 0.166/√c) quoted in the smooth_clamp entry below (1.1.0): that floor belonged to the old acosh-based arm now at VERSION_LEGACY_SMOOTHENED. The new VERSION_SMOOTHENED's floor is 2·arcsinh(10·eps)/√c ≈ 2.4e-6/√c (float32) — see the numerical-stability guide for the full version breakdown
  • lorentz_residual and lorentz_midpoint lost the Minkowski square to catastrophic cancellation at large spatial radius. Both build a raw ambient vector h and normalize it back onto the sheet by sqrt(|<h,h>_L|), and both computed <h,h>_L = -h_0^2 + ||h_s||^2 naively: for on-sheet inputs h_0 ≈ ||h_s||, so each square is ~||s||^2 (spatial radius of the inputs) while their difference is only O(1/c) — float32 relative error therefore grows as eps32 * c * ||s||^2 with eps32 ≈ 1.19e-7. Measured against float64 at c=0.1, x ≈ y, d=16 (forward / gradient relative error): 9.9e-5 / 3.0e-4 at ||s||=1e2, 6.1e-3 / 1.8e-2 at 1e3, 6.4e3 / 1.0 at 1e4 — past ||s|| ~ 1e4 the computed square flips sign, the abs() in the normalizer hides the flip, and the maximum(., 1e-7) floor silently inflates the output by 2/sqrt(1e-7) ≈ 6325× (measured 6324.6 at c=0.1, ||s||=2e4, x == y). Never a NaN, never a warning, and dormant at norm-capped activations (||s|| ≲ 20); the gradient path degrades ~3× earlier in ||s|| than the forward, from a second cancellation in the normalizer's Jacobian. Both functions now evaluate <h,h>_L through exact identities — valid for any weights given inputs on the sheet (<x,x>_L = -1/c), verified in exact rational arithmetic: for the residual h = x + w·y, <h,h>_L = -(1+w)^2/c - w·<x-y, x-y>_L; for the midpoint with reference p the vertex-nearest input, delta_m = x_m - p, W = Σ_m w_m and Delta = Σ_m w_m·delta_m, <h,h>_L = -W^2/c - W·Σ_m w_m·<delta_m, delta_m>_L + <Delta, Delta>_L. Every rounded term is now O(||x-y||^2) instead of O(||s||^2): new float32 error at ||s||=1e4 is 2.1e-5 forward / 6.0e-4 gradient (residual) and 1.6e-5 / 4.3e-4 (midpoint, M=8 softmax weights), and no regime where the old form was still usable measured worse (swept c ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1}, ||s|| from 1 to 1e5, near/far/same-direction/identical points; at ||s|| ≤ 20 old and new agree to ~2e-7 relative, not bit-identical — different rounding order). The one float32 limit that remains is the difference x - y itself: points that share a direction at ||s|| ≳ 1e4 lose it to rounding before either form sees it, and neither form is trustworthy there — that regime needs float64. For w_y >= 0 resp. non-negative weights the identities give c·|<h,h>_L| >= (1+w)^2 resp. >= W^2, so the abs() and the eps floor are now provably inactive (both kept as insurance). Affected layers: LorentzResidual, HypformerPositionalEncoding, HyperbolicFullAttention (attention aggregation and head averaging), HyperboloidGyroRMSNorm, hyperboloid frechet_mean, and any direct caller of the two functions. The LResNet reference implementation (He et al. 2025) has the same defect. Both outputs additionally have their time coordinate reconstructed from the spatial part via spatial_to_hyperboloid (x_0 = sqrt(||x_s||^2 + 1/c), the same convention as hrc/htc), so they are on-sheet by construction — as the old self-normalizing h/sqrt(-c<h,h>_L) was — even for inputs float storage cannot keep on the sheet (it needs eps·x_0^2 << 1/c, violated past ||s|| ~ 3e3 in float32 / ~1e8 in float64, e.g. a Poincaré ball-boundary point lifted to x_0 ≈ 5.5e11): the identity assumes exactly on-sheet inputs, so for those it returned a point off the sheet by 4.8e-3 and hyperboloid frechet_mean's Karcher loop diverged to NaN from it; the midpoint's reference p is now the vertex-nearest input rather than points_0, bounding every ||delta_m|| <= 2||x_m||. No API change; cost is O(1) extra for the residual and one extra einsum for the midpoint

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • hyperbolix.utils.capped_exp — exp with the argument capped at 0.99*log(finfo.max), for exp of unconstrained trainable log-scale parameters. A runaway parameter otherwise overflows to inf, which turns into NaN downstream (inf - inf in the hyperboloid time-coordinate algebra) and poisons the whole parameter tree within one optimizer step; capped_exp saturates finite instead, with a zero (not NaN) gradient past the cap. Below the cap it is a bitwise value- and gradient-identity to jnp.exp. Same idiom LearnableCurvature's "log" parameterization already used internally, now shared. Applied to the three call sites that had a bare jnp.exp on such a parameter: the Busemann FC layer's alpha = exp(log_scale), and both FHCNN/FHNN forward passes' exp(scale_val) * sigmoid(...) time-coordinate scaling

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • atanh/sinh/cosh float64 accuracy: XLA's CPU lowerings have large ulp errors that hyperbolix's wrappers previously inherited. jnp.atanh is lowered to 0.5*(log1p(x) - log1p(-x)), and XLA's CPU float64 log1p is up to ~129 ulps off for arguments in [-0.53, -0.28] (NumPy's is <1 ulp there) — atanh inherited ~129 ulp error for x in ~[0.28, 0.53], peaking at sqrt(2)-1. jnp.sinh/jnp.cosh are separately inaccurate for large arguments: ~17 ulps for |x| in [16, 512] and ~496 ulps for [512, 710] (float64; the jump sits exactly at the power-of-two boundary 512), and ~24.5 ulps in float32 across the full range. Float32 atanh was unaffected. hyperbolix.utils.math_utils.atanh is rewritten as the odd-symmetrized single-log1p identity atanh(x) = sign(x)*0.5*log1p(2|x|/(1-|x|)) (computed on |x| so the log1p argument never enters the bad window, with the sign restored via where rather than sign(x)*... — a sign-multiplied form has zero gradient at x=0, not the analytic 1). sinh is rewritten as 0.5*(expm1(x) - expm1(-x)) (cancellation-free everywhere: the two expm1 terms have opposite signs) and cosh as 0.5*(exp(x) + exp(-x)) with a custom_jvp routing its gradient to the accurate sinh form (a bare exp-form cosh's autodiff gradient is the naive cancelling sinh, inaccurate near 0). All three rewrites measure at a few ulps across their full domain (vs. the errors above) and are the same speed or faster than the builtins. Raw jnp.sinh/jnp.cosh/jnp.acosh call sites that bypassed the wrappers (the FGG spatial lift, the Busemann FC output map, the wrapped-normal log-density, and the uniform-Poincaré volume/samplers) now route through them, closing the same accuracy gap plus, in the acosh case, a singular-gradient exposure at an exact-1.0 domain boundary. No API changes; every downstream distance/logmap/MLR computation using these functions gets more accurate for free

A correctness release. A full audit of the test suite replaced shape-only checks and self-comparisons with independently transcribed NumPy/SciPy oracles, and every library defect it exposed is fixed below. No new capability beyond hyp_flatten2d; several corrections change behavior or call signatures, each marked Breaking and each with the migration in its entry.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• hyp_flatten2d (hyperbolix.nn_layers) — radius-preserving flatten of an NHWC hyperboloid feature map into one manifold point per image via Hyperboloid.log_radius_concat: (B, H, W, A) → (B, H·W·(A−1)+1). The naive alternative (reshape + hcat) inflates the expected spatial radius by ≈ √(H·W) (a 4×4 map: 4×); LogCat's digamma rescale hands the classifier head the per-pixel radius unchanged. This is the flatten step for HypConv2DHyperboloidILNN stacks feeding HypRegressionHyperboloid/FGGLorentzMLR
  • Poincare.proj_batch — batched sibling of Hyperboloid.proj_batch (arbitrary leading axes, bit-identical to vmap(proj)); HoroPCA and CO-SNE now use it instead of hand-rolled vmaps
  • hyperbolix.manifolds._base.default_atol(dtype) = sqrt(finfo(dtype).eps) — the library-wide constraint-tolerance convention (float32 3.45e-4, float64 1.49e-8) that is_in_manifold / is_in_tangent_space resolve None through on every manifold
  • HypformerPositionalEncoding accepts param_dtype and forwards it to its internal HTCLinear — float64 models were previously impossible (weights pinned to float32)
  • New exports: hcat_ambient_dim and busemann_fc_poincare_output from hyperbolix.nn_layers (both already served as test oracles and answer user-facing sizing questions); lift_ideals and orthonormalize_rows from hyperbolix.decomposition

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Hyperboloid.log_radius_concat scaled the wrong way, amplifying the spatial radius instead of preserving it. The two digamma arguments were swapped: the shipped exp(½·(ψ(N·d/2) − ψ(d/2))) is ≈ √N, so concatenating N blocks inflated the expected log spatial radius by ≈ log N — worse than the plain hcat the rescale exists to correct. The correct factor is the shrink exp(½·(ψ(d/2) − ψ(N·d/2))) ≈ 1/√N: for Gaussian spatial parts ‖v‖² ~ χ²_k gives E[log‖v‖] = ½(ψ(k/2) + log 2), so restoring the per-block value after widening d → N·d requires dividing by the ratio of the two chi radii. Nothing raised, because the mis-scaled output is still a valid manifold point (Lorentz residual ~1e-13) — only its radius was wrong. The Shi et al. 2026 reference implementation has the same sign error. Sole affected layer: HypConv2DHyperboloidILNN, where it inflated the spatial radius ≈9.4× per 3×3 conv, compounding with depth (hcat-based layers — FGG, FHNN — never used this path). Behavior change — see the coupled default-init change below
  • hyperbolix.optim.has_manifold_params always returned False. nnx.Variable is itself a registered pytree node whose single child is the raw array, so the unguarded jax.tree_util.tree_leaves call unwrapped every ManifoldParam into an ArrayImpl before the isinstance check ran — the function reported "no manifold parameters" for a bare ManifoldParam, a dict of parameters, nnx.state(model, nnx.Param) (its own documented usage) and a model alike. The traversal now stops at nnx.Variable leaves. The Riemannian optimizers were not affected: _riemannian_base already flattened with that guard everywhere it inspects Variable types, so only callers using has_manifold_params as a guard saw the false negative
